senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. זוּז)to move nimbly, hop, trip.—Pl. דִּדָּה
to walk, pull (a young child or beast unable to walk by itself).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 18:2">Sabb. XVIII, 2</cite> <he>מְדַדִּין עגלין וכ׳</he> you may lead or pull calves &c. (on the Sabbath).
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 18:2">Ib.</cite> <he>אשה מְדַדָּה וכ׳</he> a mother may walk her child. Ib. 128ᵇ <he>דוחין אין מדדין לא</he> push you may, but make them hop, no.
<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 4:7">Pes. IV, 7</cite> (<cite ref="Pesachim 55b">55ᵇ</cite>) <he>מְדַרִּין ומחזירין וכ׳</he> Ar. (ed. only <he>מחזירין</he>).
Sabb. 88ᵇ and the angels מְדַדִּין אותך led them (the frightened Israelites) back; א״ת ידודון אלא יְדַדּוּן read not (Ps. LXVIII, 13) yiddodun but y’daddun (they led them).

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:11">Cant. R. to VIII, 11</cite> the angels <he>מְדַדִּין להם וכ׳</he> led the Israelites away, <he>והיו מִדַּדִּין לפני וכ׳</he> and they themselves tripped timidly before the Lord, v. infra.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 17:2:4">Y. Sabb. XVII, end, 16ᵇ</cite>; Y. Erub. X, 26ᶜ top <he>מְדַדֵּהוּ וכ׳</he> he makes the bolt slide with his finger tips.
Cant. R. to IV, 8 [read:] אדין מְדַדֵּם ואינם וכ׳ He had just been leading them (through the Red Sea), and they should not trust?—ד׳ פיתקין to shake stones (ballots), i.e. to protest against.

<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 1:10">Esth. R. to I, 2</cite> <he>מה״ש מְדַדִּין פיתקין וכ׳</he> the angels protested against the Lord’s decision; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:11">Cant. R. to VIII, 11</cite> <he>יִדּוֹדוּן בהם ממדדין פיטקין</he> (read <he>מדדין</he>) they (the angels) were excited against them, they protested (ref. to <cite ref="Joel 4:3">Joel IV, 3</cite>).

senses.gloss: to hop, trip (of young or tied birds).
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 25b">B. Mets. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>אי מִידַּדִּין</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>אי בְמִדַּ׳</he>) if the tied birds (deposited in a certain place) hop from spot to spot.
